articles.title: From US Fed rate decision to crude oil - 3 factors that may dictate Sensex, Nifty 50 this week
articles.summary: Indian stock markets will reopen on 15 September after a holiday, with investors monitoring US interest rates, inflation data, and crude oil prices. The markets ended lower last week due to rising bond yields and inflation concerns, with the BSE Sensex declining 2.27% to 74,781.76.

articles.title: Nifty Outlook for September 15: Index move on expiry hinges on HDFC Bank, IT stocks even as oil stays higher

On the upside, 23,600-23,620 is likely to act as the immediate hurdle, while a sustained move above 23,620 could open the…
articles.why: Tuesday is also weekly expiry, and analysts say the Nifty's move hinges on HDFC Bank and IT stocks while oil stays high. Expect a volatile open as three days of global news get priced at once.

articles.title: Oversold Nifty could see a short-term rebound: Analysts
articles.summary: Indian stock indices, Sensex and Nifty, have extended their losing streak for a fifth week. Analysts suggest the indices have entered oversold territory, indicating a potential short-term rebound. Traders are advised to consider specific strategies like a Bull Put Spread for the September 29, 2026 expiry. Several…
articles.why: Analysts see the Nifty as oversold after five weekly falls and think a short-term rebound is possible, though oil, foreign selling and the Fed could cap any bounce.

articles.title: India's retail inflation quickens to 4.8% in August from 4.45% in July as food prices exert pressure
articles.summary: India's retail inflation rose to 4.82% in August 2026 from 4.45% in July. Food prices and jewellery significantly contributed to this recent inflationary pressure. The Reserve Bank of India has lowered its FY27 inflation forecast to 5%. Inflation is expected to rise in the near term and peak in the third quarter.…
articles.why: Retail inflation rose to 4.82 percent in August from 4.45 percent as food prices climbed, slightly above forecasts. It pushes the RBI further from a rate cut and keeps talk of a hike alive for the October 5-7 meeting.

articles.title: Retail inflation rises to 4.82% in August as food inflation climbs to 5.95%
articles.summary: Food inflation rose to 5.95 per cent in August from 5.52 per cent in July, while rural and urban headline inflation stood at 5.23 per cent and 4.31 per cent, respectively
articles.why: Food inflation climbed to 5.95 percent and rural inflation to 5.23 percent in August, hitting lower-income households hardest. That mix makes it harder for the RBI to look through the oil shock.

articles.title: India August Inflation Accelerates, Narrowing RBI Pause Room
articles.why: August's faster inflation narrows the RBI's room to stay on hold, Bloomberg notes, with the next policy review on October 5-7. Bond yields above 7 percent already reflect the risk of tightening.

articles.title: WPI inflation rises to 9.92% in Aug on costlier food, fuel, manufactured items
articles.summary: The August inflation print is the second highest in the new WPI series with 2022-23 as the base year
articles.why: Wholesale inflation hit 9.92 percent in August, the second highest reading in the new series, driven by fuel, food and manufactured goods. High WPI usually feeds into retail prices with a lag.

articles.title: Wholesale price inflation nears double digits in August; next month may be worse
articles.summary: High wholesale inflation feeds into retail prices as businesses and other intermediaries pass on rising input costs to final consumers. While RBI formally targets retail inflation within a 2-6% range, it closely tracks all other price indicators to determine price pressures in the economy.
articles.why: Wholesale inflation is nearing double digits and next month may be worse as businesses pass on higher input costs. That points to more retail inflation ahead and a tougher RBI in October.

articles.title: RBI Governor Malhotra calls on Finance Minister Sitharaman
articles.summary: The next meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), the RBI's rate-setting panel, is scheduled for October 5-7, 2026
articles.why: RBI Governor Malhotra met the finance minister on the day inflation data landed, with the next MPC meeting set for October 5-7. Markets will read the meeting as coordination ahead of a possible policy shift.

articles.title: FIIs sell Indian shares worth Rs 14,475 crore in Sept; analyst warns soaring bond yields may deepen selloff
articles.summary: Foreign investors sold Indian equities worth Rs 14,475 crore in September as oil prices and global bond yields surged amid escalating Middle East tensions. Analysts warned that further rises in US Treasury yields could intensify FPI outflows and pressure equities.
articles.why: Foreign investors have sold Rs 14,475 crore of Indian shares in September as oil and global yields surged. Analysts warn that a US 10-year yield above 5 percent could deepen the selling.

articles.title: BofA turns bullish on Nifty after 2 years, cautious on small, midcaps. Here's what it expects now
articles.summary: BofA Securities has turned constructive on the Nifty after two years, seeing 12% upside to 26,200 by December 2026. The brokerage said five of eight earlier risks have played out, while primary market issuances, Fed rate hikes and AI disruption remain concerns. It also turned cautious on small- and midcaps.
articles.why: BofA Securities has turned bullish on the Nifty for the first time in two years, seeing 12 percent upside to 26,200 by December, while staying cautious on small and midcaps. It is a rare positive call amid heavy foreign selling.

articles.title: Brent crude at $108: What does it mean for India and your investments?
articles.summary: Brent at $108 a barrel is certainly negative for India, but its ultimate damage depends on whether the spike is brief or sustained and whether it disrupts physical supply.
articles.why: Brent at 108 dollars raises India's import bill, pressures the rupee and squeezes oil marketing companies, airlines and paint makers. It also feeds the inflation the RBI must now respond to.

articles.title: US says it’s clearing Hormuz traffic: Why are oil futures beyond $100?
articles.summary: Brent crude crosses $107 as Hormuz disruptions and Saudi pipeline shutdown threaten global oil supply.
articles.why: Oil is above 107 dollars even as the US says it is clearing Hormuz traffic, because the Saudi pipeline shutdown and slow tanker flows keep supply tight. For India the price, not the headlines, is what matters.

articles.title: Asian shares slide as oil spike fuels inflation, rate hike concerns

articles.why: Asian shares fell as the oil spike fuelled inflation and rate hike fears, with analysts warning prices could stay elevated while Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb are under threat. A weak regional backdrop for Tuesday's reopening.

articles.title: $100 crude is an irritant, not a deal-breaker for India: Harsh Gupta Madhusudan
articles.summary: While higher oil could pressure earnings and the rupee, he argues that the impact may be less severe than feared, with India’s growth backdrop, valuations and external balances providing a buffer even as global yields and geopolitical risks remain elevated.
articles.why: One strategist argues 100 dollar crude is an irritant, not a deal-breaker, for India given its growth, valuations and external balances. The counter-view to today's gloom, worth weighing against rising inflation.

articles.title: The US Federal Reserve's policy meeting due on Wednesday, September 16; how will it impact stocks, gold, and rupee?
